mainTopic: סוכה כז. — The רבי צדוק proof, the משנה on required meals and make-up in the סוכה, and רבי אליעזר's answers to the steward of אגריפס.
overview: The גמרא finishes the story of רבי צדוק, who ate less than a כביצה outside the סוכה. It tries to use this story against רב יוסף and אביי, who allow a כביצה outside the סוכה. The proof is pushed off, because 'less than a כביצה' may be the measure for hand-washing and ברכה. Then a new משנה brings two disputes. רבי אליעזר requires fourteen meals in the סוכה, while the חכמים require only the first night. רבי אליעזר also lets a missed first-night meal be made up on the last night, while the חכמים say it is lost. The גמרא explains both sides through the idea that the סוכה is like a home. It learns the first-night obligation from a גזירה שוה ״חמשה עשר״ to מצה on פסח. It then answers that רבי אליעזר retracted the fourteen-meal view, and that the make-up is done with extra delicacies. Finally, the steward of אגריפס המלך asks רבי אליעזר two questions, and a new ברייתא of רבי אליעזר begins that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the cited source: the story of רבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its quote of the משנה. The sages had food brought up to the סוכה, but רבי צדוק ate less than a כביצה outside the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they said: 'Bring them up to the סוכה.' And when they gave רבי צדוק food that was less than a כביצה, he took it in a cloth, ate it outside the סוכה, and did not make a ברכה after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the source it began quoting earlier, so that it can use it against רב יוסף and אביי in the next step. This step is setup: the attack itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל were given small amounts of food, yet they still asked that it be brought to the סוכה. רבי צדוק, however, ate food that was less than a כביצה outside the סוכה. The detail 'less than a כביצה' is the key, because the next step will build an inference from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring them up to the סוכה
The volume of an egg, a standard halachic measure of food
He made the ברכה after eating

phrases.english: and they said: Take them up to the sukka.
phrases.notes: Said by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and רבן גמליאל about the food brought to them.

phrases.english: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok
food less than an egg-bulk,
he took it in a cloth
phrases.notes: He held it in a cloth so that he would not need to wash his hands.

phrases.english: and ate it outside the sukka
and did not recite a blessing after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source quoted on the previous עמוד as a challenge to רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.raayaObject: Whether eating a כביצה requires a סוכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's story of רבי צדוק eating less than a כביצה outside the סוכה

steps.title: Inference: a כביצה needs a סוכה, which refutes רב יוסף and אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons from the wording. If less than a כביצה may be eaten outside, then a full כביצה needs a סוכה. That seems to contradict רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that a כביצה requires a סוכה. Shall we say this is a refutation of רב יוסף and אביי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the story 'in reverse' and turns it into an attack on רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף and אביי hold that a כביצה still counts as a snack (אכילת עראי), which may be eaten outside the סוכה. The משנה stressed that רבי צדוק ate 'less than a כביצה' outside. That seems to imply a full כביצה would require a סוכה, against their view.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (introduces an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: This implies: an egg-bulk requires a sukka.
Let us say this is a refutation
of Rav Yosef and Abaye!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף וְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the source quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף and אביי, who allow eating a כביצה outside the סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה stresses 'less than a כביצה,' so a full כביצה would need a סוכה.

steps.title: Pushing off the proof: 'less than a כביצה' is about washing and ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the measure in the story may be about hand-washing and ברכה, not about סוכה. So there is no proof against רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps less than a כביצה does not require hand-washing and a ברכה, but a כביצה does require hand-washing and a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף and אביי. It offers a different reason why the משנה mentioned 'less than a כביצה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail 'less than a כביצה' explains why רבי צדוק held the food in a cloth without washing, and why he made no ברכה after it. It does not have to be about the סוכה at all. So a כביצה may still be allowed outside the סוכה, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (offers another way to read the source)
Ritual washing of the hands before eating bread
Blessing, here the blessing after eating

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'less than a כביצה' appears in the story of the סוכה, so it is easy to assume it is a סוכה measure. The דחיה says it is actually the measure for washing and ברכה.

phrases.english: Perhaps less than an egg-bulk
does not require washing and a blessing,
but an egg-bulk requires washing and a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא פָּחוֹת מִכְּבֵיצָה נְטִילָה וּבְרָכָה לָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. It does not prove רב יוסף and אביי right, but shows the source cannot refute them.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The measure 'less than a כביצה' may relate to washing and ברכה, not to the obligation of סוכה.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רב יוסף and אביי fails. The 'less than a כביצה' detail in the רבי צדוק story can be explained as a washing and ברכה measure, so eating a כביצה outside the סוכה may still be allowed.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: fourteen required meals in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. רבי אליעזר rules that one must eat fourteen meals in the סוכה, one each day and one each night.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר says a person is obligated to eat fourteen meals in the סוכה, one by day and one by night.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי אליעזר sets a fixed number of required meals in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are seven days of סוכות, and each day and each night needs one meal, which makes fourteen. In his view, eating in the סוכה is a daily obligation, not just a rule for times when one happens to eat.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Fourteen meals
a person is obligated to eat in the sukka,
one by day and one by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must eat fourteen meals in the סוכה, two for each of the seven days.

steps.title: חכמים: no fixed number, except the first night
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree. There is no set number of meals, and only the first night of the חג is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: there is no fixed number for this, except the nights of the first יום טוב of the חג alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר. They say only one meal, on the first night, is truly required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, on the other days one must eat in the סוכה only if one chooses to eat a meal. The first night is the exception, because there is a real obligation to eat a meal in the סוכה then.

keyTerms.meaning: The night of the first יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis of the הלכה that eating in the סוכה on the first night of סוכות is a definite obligation.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
there is no fixed quota for the matter,
except for the night of the first Festival day
of the Festival alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the first night's meal in the סוכה is required. Other meals are optional.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: make up the missed first-night meal on the last night
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds that if someone missed the first-night meal, he should make it up on the last night of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר also said: one who did not eat on the night of the first יום טוב should make it up on the night of the last יום טוב of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second ruling from רבי אליעזר. He allows a make-up meal (תשלומין) for the first night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'last יום טוב' is שמיני עצרת, when people no longer eat in the סוכה. Even so, רבי אליעזר holds that the missed first-night meal can be made up then.

keyTerms.meaning: The last יום טוב, which is שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: And furthermore Rabbi Eliezer said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא אָכַל [לֵילֵי] יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: One who did not eat on the night of the first Festival day —

phrases.aramaic: יַשְׁלִים לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: should compensate on the night of the last Festival day of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling of רבי אליעזר about the first-night meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed first-night meal can be made up on the night of שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: חכמים: no make-up, with a supporting פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say a missed first-night meal cannot be made up, and they cite the פסוק 'מעוות לא יוכל לתקון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: there is no making up for this, and about this it is said: 'What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי אליעזר's make-up idea. They support their view with a פסוק from קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the first-night מצוה has a fixed time. Once that time passes, the chance is lost and nothing can replace it. The פסוק describes exactly this kind of lost opportunity.

keyTerms.meaning: Make-up or compensation for a missed obligation

steps.whatToRemember: There are two disputes in this משנה. First, רבי אליעזר requires fourteen meals, while the חכמים require only the first night. Second, רבי אליעזר allows a make-up on the last night, while the חכמים say a missed first night is lost forever.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
there is no compensation for the matter,
and about this it is stated:
"That which is crooked cannot be made straight
and that which is wanting cannot be numbered."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי אליעזר's make-up ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed first-night meal in the סוכה cannot be made up.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of רבי אליעזר's ruling of fourteen meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking why רבי אליעזר requires fourteen meals. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a number, fourteen, without a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק or logic produces exactly one meal each day and one each night.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא; the discussion of the משנה begins here

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה (Step 4).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for requiring fourteen meals in the סוכה.

steps.title: Live in the סוכה the way you live at home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from ״תשבו כעין תדורו״ that you eat in the סוכה the way you eat at home: one meal by day and one by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ״תשבו״, which means ״the way you live at home.״ Just as at home a person eats one meal in the day and one at night, so too in the סוכה he eats one meal in the day and one at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר compares the סוכה to a person's regular home. At home people eat two meals a day, so the סוכה also needs two meals a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תשבו״ (you shall live) tells us the סוכה should copy normal home life. Normal home life in those days meant one meal by day and one by night. Two meals a day for seven days gives fourteen meals.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall dwell (from the פסוק ״בסכת תשבו״)
In the same way that you live (in your home)

phrases.english: "You shall dwell" means like the way you live at home.

phrases.aramaic: מָה דִּירָה — אַחַת בַּיּוֹם וְאַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה,
phrases.english: Just as in a home, one meal by day and one by night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף סוּכָּה — אַחַת בְּיוֹם וְאַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: so too in a sukka, one by day and one by night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סוכה copies the regular home schedule of two meals a day, which gives fourteen meals over seven days.

steps.title: How do the רבנן explain it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with the same comparison to a home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, how do they understand it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how the רבנן understand the comparison, since they do not require fourteen meals. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison ״כעין תדורו״ seems to support רבי אליעזר. The גמרא wants to know how the רבנן read it so that it does not require a set number of meals.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי אליעזר's reasoning to the reasoning of the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן read ״תשבו כעין תדורו״.

steps.title: At home, eating is your choice
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן agree that the סוכה is like a home. But at home nobody is forced to eat, so eating in the סוכה is also optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a home. Just as at home, if a person wants he eats and if he does not want he does not eat, so too in the סוכה, if he wants he eats and if he does not want he does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the רבנן use the same comparison to a home but draw a different lesson from it. At home there is no rule that you must eat, so there is no rule that you must eat in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the סוכה is like a home. The argument is about which part of home life the comparison teaches. רבי אליעזר takes the usual meal schedule, while the רבנן take the freedom to eat or not eat. The only rule is that when you do eat, you eat in the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wants, he does not eat

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן use the very same comparison of the סוכה to a home. They do not disagree about the source. They disagree about what the comparison teaches.

phrases.english: Like a home. Just as with a home,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי אָכֵיל אִי בָּעֵי לָא אָכֵיל,
phrases.english: if he wants he eats, if he wants he does not eat,
so too a sukka as well,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי אָכֵיל אִי בָּעֵי לָא אָכֵיל.
phrases.english: if he wants he eats, if he wants he does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by reading the same comparison in a different way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison to a home teaches that eating is optional, so there is no set number of meals.

steps.title: Then the first night should be optional too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: if eating is optional, the first night should also be optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even the first night of יום טוב should also be optional!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן's reading. Their logic seems to make every meal optional, yet they ruled in the משנה that the first night is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule ״if he wants, he eats״ has no exceptions in it. So the רבנן need a separate source to explain why the first night is different.

keyTerms.meaning: The first night of the יום טוב

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן נָמֵי!
phrases.english: even the first night of the Festival as well should be optional!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning the רבנן gave in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that the first night is required (Step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison to a home makes eating optional, nothing in it makes the first night any different.

steps.title: A word-link to פסח makes the first night required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, links סוכות to פסח through the words ״חמשה עשר״. Just as only the first night of פסח requires מצה, only the first night of סוכות requires eating in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: It says ״the fifteenth״ here, by סוכות, and it says ״the fifteenth״ by חג המצות. There, the first night is a requirement and from then on it is optional. So too here, the first night is a requirement and from then on it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a גזירה שוה, a link between two פסוקים that use the same words. Since both holidays begin on ״the fifteenth״, סוכות follows the pattern of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On פסח there is a clear rule: eating מצה is required on the first night, and after that it is optional. The shared words ״חמשה עשר״ carry the same pattern over to סוכות. So the first night is an exception that comes from a separate source, while the rest of the חג stays optional as the רבנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two פסוקים that share the same word, so a law in one applies to the other
The holiday of מצות, which is פסח

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: eating in the סוכה is optional like eating at home, except for the first night, which is required because of the גזירה שוה ״חמשה עשר״ to the first night of מצה on פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that one must eat a meal in the סוכה on the first night of סוכות, just as one must eat מצה on the first night of פסח.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
It says here "fifteenth,"
and it says "fifteenth" about the Festival of Matzot.
Just as there, the first night is an obligation,
and from then on it is optional,
so too here, the first night is an obligation,
and from then on it is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 with a separate source for the first night.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source (גזירה שוה) that creates an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since eating in the סוכה is optional like eating at home, even the first night would be optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה ״חמשה עשר״ makes the first night required, like מצה on פסח. The rest of the חג remains optional.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מצה is required on פסח night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the first-night מצה obligation, which the סוכות rule was compared to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by פסח, how do we know that eating מצה on the first night is required?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just compared the first night of סוכות to the first night of פסח. Now it asks how we know that the first night of פסח is a requirement in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison in Step 13 only works if eating מצה on פסח night is truly a חובה. If that is not proven, the comparison proves nothing. So the גמרא checks the foundation.

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: 'There' means by פסח and its מצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the foundation of the comparison made in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that eating מצה on the first night of פסח is obligatory.

steps.title: The verse 'In the evening you shall eat מצות'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״בערב תאכלו מצות״ makes eating מצה on the first night a חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'In the evening you shall eat מצות.' The Torah made it a requirement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that commands eating מצה on the evening of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses commanding language, so the first night of פסח is a fixed חובה. Through the ״חמשה עשר״ link, the first night of סוכות also becomes a חובה. Every other meal stays optional.

keyTerms.meaning: in the evening you shall eat מצות

steps.whatToRemember: The first night of סוכות is a חובה only because it is linked to the first night of פסח, where the Torah made eating מצה a requirement.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'In the evening you shall eat matzot,'
the verse established it as an obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse ״בערב תאכלו מצות״ makes eating מצה on the first night an obligation.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's make-up rule clashes with his 14-meal rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'make-up' ruling of רבי אליעזר and points out that he elsewhere requires 14 meals in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says רבי אליעזר also said that a missed first-night meal can be made up on the last night of the חג. But didn't רבי אליעזר say a person must eat 14 meals in the סוכה, one by day and one by night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, about making up a missed meal. It shows that this ruling seems to contradict another statement of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר holds that all 14 meals are required, the first night is no different from any other night. So why does his make-up ruling single out only the first night, as if it alone were a חובה? The make-up ruling seems to assume the view of the רבנן, that only the first night is required.
steps.confusionAlert: The first line here is not a new statement. It is the גמרא quoting the משנה so that it can challenge it.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said:
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about making up the missed meal.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Eliezer say
fourteen meals
a person is obligated to eat in the sukka,
one by day and one by night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה, the make-up meal.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a missed first-night meal can be made up on the last night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all 14 meals are required, the first night is not special. Yet the make-up ruling treats the first night as the one required meal, as the רבנן do.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי אמי, בירא says that רבי אליעזר retracted the 14-meal view.
steps.simpleTranslation: בירא said in the name of רבי אמי: רבי אליעזר took back his earlier view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבי אליעזר retracted the 14-meal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After he changed his mind, רבי אליעזר agrees with the רבנן that only the first night is required. Their only disagreement is whether a missed first-night meal can be made up.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who reports in the name of רבי אמי

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the whole מחלוקת. It is no longer about 14 meals. It is only about making up the required first-night meal.

phrases.english: Beira said that Rabbi Ami said:
Rabbi Eliezer retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two conflicting statements was withdrawn.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר holds both the 14-meal rule and the make-up rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר retracted the 14-meal rule and holds only the make-up rule.

steps.title: What does he make up the meal with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of food is used for the make-up meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does he make it up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the make-up actually works. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The make-up happens on שמיני עצרת, which already has its own יום טוב meal. So the גמרא wants to know what makes this food count as making up the missed meal.

phrases.english: With what does he compensate?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the view is clear, it asks how the make-up is done in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What food counts as the make-up meal.

steps.title: Bread cannot be the make-up
steps.stepSummary: Bread cannot work, because eating bread just counts as that day's own יום טוב meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he makes it up with bread, he is just eating the meal of that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible answer, bread, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שמיני עצרת a person eats a bread meal anyway for יום טוב. A bread meal would be just that day's normal meal, so nothing shows that it makes up for the missed night.

keyTerms.meaning: the meal of that day itself

phrases.english: If we say with bread,
he is eating the meal of that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to Step 18 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the make-up is done with bread.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Bread is already the required meal of שמיני עצרת, so it cannot also count as the make-up.

steps.title: He makes it up with extra delicacies
steps.stepSummary: The make-up is done by adding kinds of delicacies to the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'make up' mean? He makes it up by adding types of delicacies.
steps.whatsHappening: Since bread was rejected, the גמרא gives the real answer: extra delicacies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding special foods beyond the normal יום טוב meal shows that something extra is being eaten for the missed night. The extra food is what marks it as a make-up.

keyTerms.meaning: kinds of delicacies or side dishes

phrases.english: Rather, what is meant by 'he should compensate'?
He compensates with types of delicacies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after bread was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The make-up is done by adding extra delicacies.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the delicacies answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that adding delicacies fulfills the make-up.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: if he made it up with types of delicacies, he fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what it just answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 20 is no longer just reasoning. A source from the תנאים states it directly.

phrases.english: That is also taught in a baraita:
If he compensated with types of delicacies, he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the make-up is done with delicacies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: אם השלים במיני תרגימא יצא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, a missed first-night meal is made up on the last night by adding extra delicacies, not by an ordinary bread meal.

steps.title: The steward asks whether one meal a day is enough
steps.stepSummary: The steward of אגריפס המלך asks רבי אליעזר whether, since he normally eats only one meal a day, one meal in the סוכה is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The steward of King אגריפס asked רבי אליעזר: someone like me, who usually eats only one meal a day, may I eat one meal and be exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a man who asks whether the two-meals-a-day rule applies to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steward's question assumes רבי אליעזר's earlier view that one must eat one meal by day and one by night. The steward argues that because the סוכה is 'like a home', and he eats only once a day at home, one meal should be enough.

phrases.english: The steward of King Agrippas asked
Rabbi Eliezer:
Someone like me, who is not accustomed
to eat more than one meal a day,
what is the law: may I eat one meal and be exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story connected to רבי אליעזר's meal requirement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person who normally eats one meal a day may eat only one meal in the סוכה.

steps.title: Add a little extra in honor of your Creator
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the steward eats many snacks for his own pleasure, so he should add one for his Creator's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Every day you eat many little appetizers for your own enjoyment. Now you won't add even one appetizer in honor of your Maker?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר rejects the steward's request and tells him to add at least a small extra food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a person who eats 'one meal' a day keeps snacking on extras for his own pleasure. So he can surely add one small extra for the מצוה. This also fits the earlier idea that extra small foods can count toward a required meal.
steps.whatToRemember: A personal habit does not excuse a person from honoring the מצוה. If you add extras for yourself, add something for your Creator too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Each and every day you continue eating
several appetizers in your own honor,
and now you will not continue with
one appetizer in honor of your Maker?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם אַתָּה מַמְשִׁיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the steward's question from Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One meal is not enough. He must add at least one small extra food for the honor of his Maker.

steps.title: The steward asks about switching between two סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The steward has a wife and a סוכה in טבריא and another wife and סוכה in ציפורי. He asks whether he may move from one סוכה to the other and still fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him another question: Someone like me has two wives, one in טבריא and one in ציפורי, and two סוכות, one in each city. May I go from one סוכה to the other and still fulfill my obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The same steward from the last step asks רבי אליעזר a second question. This time it is about using two different סוכות during one festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first question was about how many meals he must eat in the סוכה. This question is about place: must the מצוה be done in one סוכה, or can it be split between two? His life naturally moves between two homes, so he wants to know if his סוכה can move with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, a city in the Galil
Tzippori, another city in the Galil
What is the law? (a question formula)
And I will be exempt, meaning I will have fulfilled my obligation

phrases.english: And he further asked him:
phrases.notes: The steward of אגריפס המלך is still speaking to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אֲנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים,
phrases.english: For someone like me, who has two wives,
one in Tiberias and one in Tzippori,
and I have two sukkot,
one in Tiberias and one in Tzippori,
what is the law: may I go from sukkah to sukkah and be exempt?
phrases.notes: He wants to spend part of the festival in one סוכה and part in the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question from the same steward, moving from how much he must eat in the סוכה to whether he may use two סוכות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may fulfill the מצוה of סוכה by moving between two different סוכות during the festival.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר forbids switching סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers no. In his view, whoever moves from one סוכה to another cancels the מצוה of the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No! For I say: Anyone who goes from one סוכה to another has cancelled the מצוה of the first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the steward's question with a clear "no." He explains that switching to a second סוכה ruins the מצוה of the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the מצוה is to live in one סוכה for the whole festival, the way a person lives in one home. If you leave it for a different סוכה, the first סוכה no longer counts as your festival home. This is רבי אליעזר's own view, and it fits his strict approach seen in the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: For I say (introduces the speaker's reason)
One who goes out or leaves
The מצוה of the first סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as "you may never leave your סוכה." The issue is replacing it with a different סוכה. Also, this is רבי אליעזר's personal view. It is not the accepted הלכה, which permits moving between סוכות.

phrases.english: He said to him: No!
For I say:
Anyone who goes from one sukkah to another sukkah
has cancelled the מצוה of the first.
phrases.notes: According to רבי אליעזר, one must stay in the same סוכה for all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the steward's question from Step 24 with a negative ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Moving to a second סוכה cancels the מצוה of the first, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, for רבי אליעזר, the מצוה of סוכה is tied to one fixed dwelling for the whole festival, not just to sitting in any סוכה.
steps.whatToRemember: The steward asked two questions. First, can one meal a day in the סוכה be enough? רבי אליעזר said to add one for his Creator's honor. Second, may he switch between two סוכות? רבי אליעזר said no, because switching cancels the first סוכה's מצוה.

steps.title: Introducing a new ברייתא from רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר states another ruling. The ruling itself continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is about to quote another ruling of רבי אליעזר from a ברייתא, and the content comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תניא signals that a teaching from the time of the תנאים is being brought. The גמרא is continuing its collection of רבי אליעזר's views about סוכה. So far this line only names the speaker; the actual ruling has not been stated yet.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: The ruling itself continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of the steward ends, the גמרא opens a new ברייתא with more of רבי אליעזר's rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. This line only introduces a ruling of רבי אליעזר that continues on the next עמוד.
